record.program_name: Local Government Special Needs Housing Program (SNHP)
record.administering_agency: California Housing Finance Agency (CalHFA), with county MHSA funds
record.typical_award_size: Historically county-funded MHSA capital loans and capitalized operating subsidies administered by CalHFA (16 participating counties as of 2019).
record.affordability_requirement: Permanent supportive housing units for persons with serious mental illness eligible for MHSA services.
record.next_deadline: Program discontinued effective January 3, 2020 per DHCS Information Notice 19-047; no new rounds.
record.layering_notes: No live CalHFA program page exists; the CalHFA multifamily programs page (source) no longer lists SNHP, and a DHCS notice (BH-IN-19-047) states CalHFA discontinued the program effective Jan 3, 2020 with county MHSA funds reverting to county control. Marked needs_confirmation because the DHCS notice could not be opened this pass. Successor supportive housing capital now comes from Homekey+, HCD MHP supportive units, and county Behavioral Health Services Act (Prop 1) housing allocations (research in Pass 2). CTCAC still lists SNHP commitments as qualifying homeless-assistance funding in the nonprofit set-aside.
record.audit_note: No SNHP guidelines or term sheet are readable (CalHFA program page omits SNHP and legacy SNHP paths return 404), so the value stays unclear on the general Labor Code 1720 rule.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. No SNHP program document could be read: the CalHFA multifamily programs page (https://www.calhfa.ca.gov/multifamily/programs/index.htm) no longer lists SNHP, and the former CalHFA SNHP and MHSA program and term sheet paths return 404, so no stated wage rule was found. SNHP capital loans of county MHSA funds are public funds under 1720(b) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720); a below-market residual receipts loan on a project with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI can be exempt under 1720(c)(5)(E) (https://dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2020/2019-018.pdf), and capitalized operating subsidies are not construction. Program discontinued effective January 3, 2020.

record.program_name: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (County Code Chapter 8-8), in-lieu fee and the Affordable Housing Program account, unincorporated Yolo County
record.administering_agency: Yolo County Community Services Department, Planning Division (ordinance and affordable housing agreements); in-lieu fees held by the County in the Affordable Housing Program account
record.typical_award_size: Regulatory requirement, not a funding source. Ordinance 1451 (effective January 1, 2015) requires on-site affordable units: for-sale projects of 10 or more units set aside 20% (half low income, half moderate income); rental projects of 20 or more units set aside 25% very low income plus 10% low income; rental projects of 7 to 19 units set aside 15% very low plus 10% low. Smaller projects (9 or fewer single-family, 7 or fewer multifamily) pay an in-lieu fee assessed on a unit percentage basis. The in-lieu fee equals a percentage of the estimated cost to construct the required units, is set in the County Master Fee Schedule (last adopted June 24, 2025) and may be reduced up to 50% based on available subsidy; the current per-unit amount was not published in the opened documents (the 2009 schedule was $12,920 for-sale and $17,610 rental per required unit).
record.affordability_requirement: Rental inclusionary units must be permanently affordable (Sec. 8-8.108(b)); for-sale units carry a 20-year covenant that resets at each resale to a qualified buyer. Alternatives, only if on-site is shown infeasible: off-site units in the unincorporated county, land dedication (2 acres minimum), in-lieu fee, or housing credits transferable within 3 miles and 5 years. Density bonus units do not generate an inclusionary obligation.
record.next_deadline: Applies at discretionary approval; fee estimate given at approval and paid before final map, first building permit or certificate of occupancy. In-lieu fees must be spent or encumbered within five years of receipt unless the Board extends.
record.layering_notes: The Affordable Housing Program account (Sec. 8-8.116) is the County's only local housing fund and it is fed solely by in-lieu fees from small unincorporated projects, so expect a balance in the low hundreds of thousands at most; no NOFA or award from it was found. For a 100% affordable project the ordinance imposes no obligation and offers the incentives in Sec. 8-8.118 (fee waiver, standards modifications, streamlining, density bonus). For a mixed-income rental project of 20 or more units the 35% combined set-aside (25% very low plus 10% low) is one of the steepest in the region and is a real feasibility constraint in Esparto, Madison and Dunnigan; the ordinance predates current state density bonus law and the Latinos Unidos v. Napa decision, so confirm how the County applies it today. Davis, Woodland and West Sacramento have their own inclusionary programs (Davis in-lieu fee about $215,000 per unit) covered in Pass 3.
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: Sections 8-8.106 to 8-8.111 (Ord. 1451, effective January 1, 2015: 20% for-sale at 10+ units split low and moderate, 25% very low plus 10% low at 20+ rental units, 15% plus 10% at 7 to 19 units, in-lieu fee below 7 multifamily or 10 single-family units, permanent rental and 20-year resetting for-sale covenants, alternatives only if on-site is infeasible, 2-acre minimum dedication, credits within 3 miles and 5 years) match the zoneomics mirror only; amlegal and yolocounty.gov return 403. Mirror-only source does not support verified. funding_type moved from density bonus to regulatory requirement per SCHEMA.md (inclusionary).
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) reaches only construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, and 1720(c)(1) exempts private residential projects on private property unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment or successor agency, or local public housing authority; this inclusionary ordinance (County Code Chapter 8-8) provides no public funds, so it does not by itself trigger prevailing wage. Any public loan, grant, land write-down or fee waiver layered on a project is assessed separately under 1720(b). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

record.program_name: Tax-exempt multifamily bonds: no County or YCH conduit program; CMFA and CSCDA issuances with local TEFRA approval
record.administering_agency: Issuers California Municipal Finance Authority and California Statewide Communities Development Authority; TEFRA approval by the host city council or, in the unincorporated area, the Yolo County Board of Supervisors
record.typical_award_size: Project-sized conduit issuances. Example: CMFA issued $6,668,698 of tax-exempt bonds for Esperanza Crossing Apartments (Mercy Housing, 40 units on Woodland Avenue, 39 units at or below 55% AMI). No County of Yolo or Yolo County Housing bond issuance and no County TEFRA resolution appeared in the 2026 Board minutes reviewed (January 27, March 3 and March 24, 2026).
record.affordability_requirement: Federal bond and 4% LIHTC rules: at least 20% of units at 50% AMI or 40% at 60% AMI (or income averaging), 55-year CDLAC regulatory agreement.
record.next_deadline: Request the TEFRA hearing through the issuer; allow six to eight weeks before the CDLAC application. For unincorporated sites the hearing goes on a Board of Supervisors consent agenda; for Davis, Woodland and West Sacramento sites the city council holds it (Pass 3).
record.layering_notes: Neither the County nor YCH runs a bond program, so budget issuer fees for CMFA or CSCDA. Bonds alone do not trigger state prevailing wage, but tax credits plus state or County funds in the same deal usually do. The County's TEFRA practice in the unincorporated area could not be confirmed from opened documents because no recent unincorporated bond-financed project was found.
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: old CMFA ?p=2377 link redirects to the Esperanza Crossing news page, which confirms $6,668,698 CMFA tax-exempt financing, 40 units on Woodland Avenue in Yolo County, 39 units at or below 55% AMI for 55 years. The County Board minutes claims were not re-opened and no stated prevailing wage rule for conduit bonds alone was found, so prevailing_wage_trigger stays unclear.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: False for the conduit bond financing itself. DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, Public Works Case No. 2006-020, Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe, held that privately placed and publicly offered conduit housing revenue bonds are not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b) because the issuer never holds the proceeds or repayments, and that federal LIHTCs are not public funds (https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf; https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720). The CMFA Esperanza Crossing release states no wage term (https://www.cmfa-ca.com/mercy-housing-preserves-affordable-housing-using-tax-exempt-financing-issued-cmfa/), and a County or city TEFRA approval adds no public funds. Other public sources in the same deal (City or County loans, land, HOME at 12 or more HOME-assisted units, PBVs at 9 or more assisted units) are tested separately and can trigger state or federal prevailing wage.

record.program_name: City of Davis Housing Trust Fund (in-lieu fees and negotiated developer contributions, Article 18.05)
record.administering_agency: City of Davis Social Services and Housing Department (Housing Trust Fund administered by the Affordable Housing Manager; Social Services Commission reviews affordable housing plans)
record.typical_award_size: Project-specific gap contributions sized by Council; no published NOFA or guidelines found. Revenue is in-lieu fees under Resolution 25-002 ($250,000 per unit) plus negotiated contributions from peripheral Measure J/R/D projects: Village Farms Exhibit E (approved December 16, 2025, revised January 13, 2026) commits $6,000,000 to the Housing Trust Fund ($2 million with dedication of the first land site, $1 million at the first building permit, $3 million before any Phase 3 building permit); Willowgrove's plan reportedly adds $1.8 million. Earlier years the fund was small (the 2023 single-family in-lieu fee was about $82,000 per unit) and the City has historically funded projects such as Paul's Place and Creekside from it. Current balance not published in any document opened this pass.
record.affordability_requirement: Low and very low income units with long-term covenants; Council direction prioritizes very low and extremely low income and deed-restricted ownership.
record.next_deadline: No NOFA. Contributions arrive with Village Farms and Willowgrove milestones only if voters approved the projects (Village Farms was placed on the June 2026 ballot and Willowgrove on the November 2026 ballot); verify election outcomes and timing with the Affordable Housing Manager, (530) 757-5602.
record.layering_notes: The only local soft money in Davis. Sized to projects on the dedicated land sites first (the Village Farms plan says the money should support affordable housing on the dedication sites but may be used elsewhere consistent with the plan). Local and state funds are public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so state prevailing wage applies unless a 1720(c) exemption fits the deal, such as 1720(c)(5)(E) for below-market loans with at least 40 percent of units restricted 20 years at or below 80 percent AMI (see prevailing_wage_basis). Councilmembers raised formalizing the fund into a structured trust (April 2026). Davis has no RDA successor housing fund. Blocked: cityofdavis.org pages and the Village Farms Exhibit E staff reports (403); facts are from the December 16, 2025 and January 13, 2026 Council minutes on documents.cityofdavis.org, which did open.
record.audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true rested on public-funds logic only; no program or local rule found, changed to unclear.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. No City of Davis Housing Trust Fund NOFA, guideline, resolution or loan term requiring prevailing wage was found (no published guidelines exist; the December 16, 2025 Council minutes have no wage term). Loans are public funds under 1720(b)(1) or (b)(4), but qualifying below-market loans may be exempt under 1720(c)(5)(E) and small subsidies under 1720(c)(3). https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

record.program_name: Affordable housing land dedication sites under Article 18.05 (Village Farms 16-acre dedication, Project Individualized Plan Exhibit E)
record.administering_agency: City of Davis Community Development Department and Social Services and Housing Department (Council subcommittee negotiates development agreements)
record.typical_award_size: Land, not cash. Village Farms Davis (Development Agreement Exhibit E, approved December 16, 2025 and revised January 13, 2026) dedicates 16 acres to the City for 280 low and very low income units on fully improved sites (no more than 4 parcels, none under 2.5 acres), to be developed with a qualified affordable housing developer selected by the City, with the City to endeavor to add 80 moderate income units. Baseline features now require construction to commence on 100 affordable units before Phase 3 and no permits beyond the first 150 until that starts; the City holds an option after 150 units. Together with the $6 million Housing Trust Fund payment the package is valued by the applicant at over $6 million plus land.
record.affordability_requirement: 280 low and very low income units (plus up to 80 moderate) on dedicated land; affordability covenants set in the City's developer agreement.
record.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. Village Farms dedication will not proceed after the reported Measure V defeat; watch for a revised application or other Article 18.05 dedications.
record.layering_notes: This is how 100% affordable developers get sites in Davis: the inclusionary ordinance's land dedication option plus Housing Trust Fund money, then compete for 9% credits, MHP, AHSC or HCD Super NOFA money. Vice Mayor Vaitla's December 2025 direction to amend the land dedication option (so dedicators also provide resources) led to a March 2026 ordinance introduction, so later projects should carry cash with the land. Earlier dedications (Cannery, Chiles Ranch, Bretton Woods) produced sites now built or in pipeline. Davis has no city-owned surplus land program beyond these dedications. Pair with Yolo County Housing PBVs and the CoC HHAP money for supportive units.
record.cycle_notes: Village Farms land dedication approved by Council December 16, 2025 (revised January 13, 2026) depended on voter approval under Measure J/R/D; press reports say Measure V failed June 2, 2026, so the dedication will not occur unless the project returns. The general Article 18.05 land dedication option still exists.
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: reclassified other to land (dedicated land is the value to the project). Minutes facts re-confirmed. Measure V (Village Farms) failed at the June 2, 2026 election per press reports of the certified count (11,414 yes, 11,690 no; Davis Enterprise and Davis Vanguard); no official Yolo County statement of vote was opened, so confirm.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. The January 13, 2026 City Council minutes on the Village Farms Exhibit E affordable housing plan (https://documents.cityofdavis.org/Media/CityCouncil/Documents/PDF/CityCouncil/CouncilMeetings/Minutes/2026/Minutes-2026-01-13-City-Council-Meeting.pdf) state no wage rule, and no Davis land dedication or developer agreement term on prevailing wage was found. Land the City receives under Article 18.05 and later conveys to an affordable developer for less than fair market price is public funds under 1720(b)(3) (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720), so coverage turns on the conveyance terms, the 1720(c) exemptions and the project's other public funds.

record.program_name: Density bonus (Davis Municipal Code Section 40.27.110, deviations under Article 18.05 and state density bonus law)
record.administering_agency: City of Davis Community Development Department, Planning Division
record.typical_award_size: Regulatory. Section 40.27.110 (Ordinance 2322, 2008) allows deviations from zoning standards in accordance with the density bonuses and incentives provided for affordable housing by Article 18.05 and state density bonus law (Government Code 65915). Davis has no local enhancement beyond the state schedule; Article 18.05 alternatives (in-lieu fee, land dedication) are the local layer.
record.affordability_requirement: State density bonus law thresholds (5% very low, 10% low, 100% affordable up to 80% bonus and unlimited near transit) or Article 18.05 inclusionary units.
record.next_deadline: None; applied with the entitlement application. Davis is updating its General Plan (2025 to 2027), which may fold density bonus text into a zoning rewrite.
record.layering_notes: Standard state law implementation; Davis downtown zones (Article 40.13) are form-based and the 2021-2029 Housing Element rezoned sites to meet RHNA, so the bonus matters most on R-3 and R-HD infill sites. Davis is not Prohousing designated. No fee waiver program for affordable units exists at the City level; development impact fees are set by Council annually. The code mirror (zoneomics) was used because qcode.us is blocked; confirm against the official code.
record.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: Section 40.27.110 (Ord. 2322) text matches the zoneomics mirror only; qcode.us and cityofdavis.org are blocked. Mirror-only source does not support verified.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Labor Code 1720(a)(1) (california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720): public works means construction paid for in whole or in part out of public funds. A density bonus under Gov. Code 65915 grants units, concessions and waivers of standards, not public funds, so the bonus itself does not trigger prevailing wage. Wages may still apply through other public financing or through streamlining laws that require them (for example SB 423 or AB 2011).

record.program_name: CDBG and HOME entitlement allocations (2025-2029 Consolidated Plan, Resolution 25-061) and PLHA formula allocation
record.administering_agency: City of Davis Social Services and Housing Department, Housing and Grants Management (Director Dana Bailey)
record.typical_award_size: Davis is a CDBG entitlement city and a HOME participating jurisdiction. Council adopted the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and the Program Year One (2025) Annual Action Plan on April 15, 2025 (Resolution 25-061). Local coverage puts year one CDBG plus HOME at about $1.06 million; HOME has historically funded first-time homebuyer loans and rental project gap loans, CDBG funds public services, facilities and the Pathways to Employment and homelessness programs. HCD's 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA lists Davis at about $1.33 million over five years; staff told Council on February 18, 2025 that PLHA would be used for homeownership opportunities.
record.per_unit_cap: HOME per-unit subsidy limits apply (HUD 221(d)(3) limits for Yolo County).
record.affordability_requirement: CDBG at or below 80% AMI; HOME at or below 80% AMI with at least 90% of rental assistance at 60% AMI and 20% of units at 50% AMI in projects with 5 or more HOME units.
record.next_deadline: Program Year 2026-27 Action Plan process runs winter to spring 2027 (public hearing typically April). Confirm amounts and the HOME set-aside with the Grants Management office, (530) 757-5602.
record.layering_notes: Federal money is the only recurring Davis source for rental projects, but the annual HOME amount is small (hundreds of thousands) and competes with homebuyer uses; combine with Housing Trust Fund gap money and state credits. Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units or 8 or more CDBG-assisted units; state prevailing wage turns on the local or state funds in the deal and the Labor Code 1720(c) exemptions (see prevailing_wage_basis). Davis also receives HHAP through the Davis, Woodland/Yolo County CoC (see county record) for supportive housing operations. Yolo County's own CDBG and HOME (state non-entitlement) cover only unincorporated areas, so there is no overlap. Blocked: the Grants Management page and the Consolidated Plan PDF on cityofdavis.org (403); the April 15, 2025 minutes on documents.cityofdavis.org were opened and record the adoption.
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: April 15, 2025 minutes confirm Resolution 25-061 adopting the 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan and Year One CDBG and HOME Action Plan, but the $1.06 million year one amount and $1.33 million PLHA figure come from press and the HCD NOFA, not an opened source; cityofdavis.org still 403. Next action plan cycle label should read Program Year 2027 (hearing expected spring 2027).
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: West Sacramento Housing Trust Fund (Fund 261-9385) gap financing loans, HOME program income and City land contributions
record.administering_agency: City of West Sacramento Economic Development and Housing Department, Housing Division (Housing Manager Raul Huerta; Community Investment Principal Planner David Tilley, (916) 617-4661)
record.typical_award_size: Project-sized gap loans from Chapter 15.40 in-lieu receipts, used for gap financing to projects with affordable units, infrastructure supporting affordable housing and predevelopment. Most recent example (developer fact sheet, not a City document): The Bridge at West Gateway / West Gateway Place II (60 units, 20% to 60% AMI, six PSH units at 20% AMI, opened June 2025) received $5,194,626 from the City Housing Trust Fund, $2,000,000 of City HOME program income and City land valued at $3,344,500 alongside $11.17 million HCD MHP and $24.76 million California Housing Accelerator. Earlier: $1,191,428 of CDBG program income for West Gateway Place Phase 1 infrastructure and $2.6 million AHSC. Fund balance not published in documents opened this pass.
record.per_unit_cap: None published; West Gateway Place II implies roughly $87,000 per unit of trust fund money plus land.
record.affordability_requirement: Very low and low income rental units with 55-year covenants; Housing Element priority for extremely low income and large family units in the Bridge District, Washington and Grand Gateway areas.
record.next_deadline: No NOFA; the City negotiates commitments with its development partners (Jamboree with the West Sacramento Housing Development Corporation, Mercy Housing, New Hope CDC) ahead of state rounds. Ask the Housing Division for the current Fund 261 balance and the Grand Gateway affordable site schedule.
record.layering_notes: West Sacramento is the most active city funder in Yolo County: City land plus trust fund plus HOME program income have repeatedly made 100% affordable Bridge District projects competitive for MHP, Accelerator and AHSC (MOSA won $43 million AHSC in December 2025). The structure is a subordinate residual receipts loan plus ground lease or land conveyance. Layer order: AHSC or MHP, 4% bonds and credits (CMFA or CSCDA conduit with City TEFRA), Yolo County Housing PBVs, City trust fund, PLHA, CDBG for infrastructure. Successor agency land and EIFD financing are separate records. Blocked: cityofwestsacramento.org Housing Division pages, the Housing Policies and Studies page and the SB 341 report (403); the Legistar API only holds 2019 to 2022 matters and the Granicus feed is empty; the City now posts agendas on its own site. Facts are from the HCD-hosted 2021-2029 Housing Element plus the Jamboree fact sheet.
record.audit_note: Audit 2026-11-08: Housing Element confirms the Housing Trust Fund (Fund 261-9385) and its uses (gap loans, infrastructure for affordable housing, predevelopment) and the WSHDC, Mercy and Jamboree partnerships, but the West Gateway Place II dollar figures come only from the Jamboree fact sheet; cityofwestsacramento.org still returns 403 and the Granicus archive is empty.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal rules by name: HOME, 24 CFR 92.354 (law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/92.354), Davis-Bacon wages apply when 12 or more units are HOME-assisted; CDBG, Housing and Community Development Act sec. 110 (42 U.S.C. 5310), Davis-Bacon applies to CDBG-financed construction, and for residential property only at 8 or more units. Below those thresholds federal wages do not apply; state prevailing wage may still apply under Labor Code 1720 depending on 1720(c) exemptions (single-family rehab and homebuyer aid are exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C)).

record.program_name: Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) formula funds, Resolution 25-15 five-year plan
record.administering_agency: City of West Sacramento Economic Development and Housing Department, Housing Division (Housing Manager Raul Huerta)
record.typical_award_size: Council adopted Resolution 25-15 on February 19, 2025 (5 to 0) authorizing the PLHA application and a five-year plan for $763,253 of 2021, 2022 and 2023 formula allocations: 55% ($419,789) for the affordable housing component of the Grand Gateway Master Plan, specifically a proposed 114-unit affordable project serving households at 30%, 50%, 60% and up to 80% AMI; 40% ($305,301) for owner-occupied rehabilitation grants up to $30,000 through existing nonprofit contracts; 5% administration. HCD's 2024-2028 PLHA NOFA lists West Sacramento at about $1.04 million over the next five years. The City filed a CEQA notice of exemption for the plan on February 19, 2025.
record.affordability_requirement: Rental component at or below 80% AMI with deeper targeting (30% to 60% AMI) at the Grand Gateway site; owner rehabilitation for low income owners in qualifying neighborhoods.
record.next_deadline: The Grand Gateway affordable project has no published developer selection or construction date; later PLHA years (2024 onward) need a plan amendment. Verify with the Housing Division.
record.layering_notes: Small but useful: about $420,000 earmarked to one City-sponsored project in the Grand Gateway District (City-owned land, see successor agency record). Any developer of that site should expect PLHA plus Housing Trust Fund plus land, then compete for MHP or AHSC. PLHA states no wage rule of its own; construction use is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), subject to the 1720(c) exemptions (see prevailing_wage_basis). Yolo County's own PLHA is unincorporated only. Source is the state CEQA notice of exemption filed by the City; the resolution and staff report on cityofwestsacramento.org returned 403, and dollar figures are from local press coverage of the February 19, 2025 meeting.
record.audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true rested on public-funds logic only; no program or local rule found, changed to unclear.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. HCD 2024-2028 PLHA Formula Guidelines and Formula Allocation NOFA contain no prevailing wage provision; no West Sacramento plan term adding prevailing wage was found. The 40% owner-occupied rehabilitation grants are single-family rehab exempt under 1720(c)(5)(C). https://www.hcd.ca.gov/sites/default/files/docs/grants-and-funding/plha/2024-2028-plha-formula-guidelines.pdf

record.program_name: Redevelopment Successor Agency housing assets, Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District and City-owned land (Grand Gateway Master Plan area, Bridge District, Washington Specific Plan)
record.administering_agency: City of West Sacramento as Housing Successor and Redevelopment Successor Agency (Economic Development and Housing Department; Yolo Countywide Successor Agency Oversight Board)
record.typical_award_size: Land and tax increment tools rather than a cash fund. With the loss of redevelopment the City repealed Chapter 15.10 and formed an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District with 14 project areas that, with Measure G sales tax, funds infrastructure for infill, high-density, transit-oriented housing in the riverfront districts (Community Investment Program HE-PR-1.4). The City owns the Grand Gateway Master Plan area (former West Capitol Avenue redevelopment parcels; the Oversight Board approved sale of three Successor Agency parcels at 485 Lighthouse Drive and 2400 and 2600 West Capitol Avenue to the City for $1,310,000 in 2024) where a 114-unit affordable project is planned, and has contributed land to West Gateway Place I and II in the Bridge District. Housing successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund balance and SB 341 reports were not accessible this pass.
record.affordability_requirement: LMIHAF uses follow Health and Safety Code 34176.1 (30% of spending at or below 30% AMI, remainder at or below 60% AMI, 55-year covenants); City land deals carry negotiated covenants.
record.next_deadline: Unknown, verify with agency. Watch for a developer solicitation for the Grand Gateway affordable site and for the annual SB 341 housing successor report (due by April 1 with the APR).
record.layering_notes: West Sacramento is the only Yolo County city with an active successor agency land program and an EIFD; the brief's note that it has active successor programs is confirmed in the Housing Element but current LMIHAF numbers could not be read. Developers should ask the Housing Division about (1) City-owned sites in Grand Gateway, Washington and Bridge District, (2) EIFD or Measure G infrastructure contributions that reduce off-site costs, and (3) any LMIHAF balance for extremely low income units. Layer with the Housing Trust Fund, PLHA and state AHSC (the 2016 to 2021 cycle brought $4.13 million AHSC infrastructure plus $2.6 million for West Gateway Place). Blocked: cityofwestsacramento.org and yolocounty.gov (403); the Oversight Board facts come from search snippets of Yolo County documents, so confirm.
record.audit_note: PW citation pass Nov 9, 2026: true rested on public-funds logic only; no program or local rule found, changed to unclear.
record.prevailing_wage_basis: Only the general Labor Code 1720(b) definition applies; outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts. City or Successor Agency land conveyed below fair market value is public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(3); 1720(c)(4) names only the former redevelopment Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund, not housing successor asset funds; EIFD-funded public infrastructure is itself public works, but its effect on a private housing project depends on 1720(c)(2) and (c)(3). No disposition or EIFD term requiring prevailing wage on the housing was found. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720

record.program_name: CDBG entitlement program (2026-2030 Consolidated Plan) and HOME program income
record.administering_agency: City of West Sacramento Economic Development and Housing Department, Housing Division
record.typical_award_size: West Sacramento became a CDBG entitlement city in FY 2016/17 and receives about $546,000 a year (the City's March 2026 notice anticipated an amount similar to the prior year's $546,333). The draft 2026-2030 Consolidated Plan and FY 2026-27 Annual Action Plan were out for comment March 6 to April 7, 2026. Housing uses have been infrastructure for affordable projects ($1,191,428 of CDBG program income for West Gateway Place Phase 1), fair housing services, homeless coordinator staffing, first-time homebuyer help and owner rehabilitation. The City is not a HOME participating jurisdiction but holds HOME program income from earlier state HOME awards ($2,000,000 went into West Gateway Place II).
